title: The Photograph Nobody Recognised
subtitle: 摄影影像 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 摄影影像（文学艺术与体育·摄影与记录）
meta: 主题语境：摄影影像（文学艺术与体育·摄影与记录）　|　核心词汇：image　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 image 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1994 a box of glass plates was found behind a wall in our town hall, and for eleven weeks the local paper printed one ① image a week. Nobody could ② image what the box was doing there, least of all the council, which had sold the building twice. What the plates showed was the same street, taken from the same window, at intervals nobody had recorded. Every image in that box, the photographer must have thought, would be read by somebody.

I was given the job of cataloguing them, which meant dates, and dates were the difficulty. There was no ③ image of a clock in any of them and no ④ image of a newspaper either, but in the eleventh plate a shop sign had changed, and the shop's records fixed the year at 1911. Everything else was dated outwards from that.

The ⑤ image people remembered, once it was printed, was not a street at all but a girl on a bicycle who appears in four plates and never looks at the camera. She became, in about a month, the town's ⑥ image of itself: cheerful, unhurried, slightly out of focus. Nobody knew her name, and nobody minded, which says more about 1911 than about her.

What the plates could not show was what happened between them. A photograph is an ⑦ image and not an argument; it proves that a thing was somewhere, never that it was fine. I wrote that in the catalogue and was asked to remove it, and I did not remove it, and the ⑧ image of the archive, which had been hoping for something celebratory, cooled noticeably.

The image of that street has since been reprinted nine times. The box went to the county record office in 1996 and I have not seen it since. What stays with me is the ⑨ image on plate eleven: the girl, the bicycle, and behind her the same street doubled in the shop window. An ⑩ image, I have concluded, is the most patient metaphor there is: it waits on a piece of glass for eighty years, and then says nothing at all.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 图像；照片；画面
B. n. 形象；印象；看法（the image of）
C. n. 影像；映像（玻璃板、胶片上的）
D. v. 想象；设想（image sth）
E. n. （镜面、玻璃中的）映像；倒影
F. 固定搭配：an image of a clock 钟的图像／画面
G. n. 声誉；公众形象（public image）
H. n. 意象；比喻（修辞上的形象化说法）

items.q: Nobody could image what the box was doing there
There was no image of a clock
no image of a newspaper either
A photograph is an image and not an argument
the same street doubled in the shop window
An image, I have concluded, is the most patient metaphor

answers.why: 指印在报上的“照片、图像”，说每周登一张。
image 作动词（罕见用法），意为“想象、设想”，说没人能想出那箱子为何在那儿。
an image of a clock 意为“钟的图像”，说所有照片里都没有钟可辨年份。
同样指画面内容，说也没有任何报纸的画面。
指人们记住的那一幅“画面”——骑自行车的女孩，而不是街道。
the town's image of itself 意为“小镇对自己的形象、看法”。
指照片作为“影像”本身，说影像只能证明某物在某处，不能证明一切安好。
指档案馆的“形象、声誉”，说它原本指望有点可庆祝的东西，因而态度转冷。
指橱窗玻璃里的“映像、倒影”，说同一条街在橱窗里被映成了双份。
image 指修辞上的“意象、比喻”，说影像是最有耐心的比喻：在玻璃上等了八十年什么也不说。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 连续十一周，当地报纸每周登一张照片。（image）
没人能想出那只箱子为什么会在那儿。（image v.）
所有照片里都没有钟的画面可用来断代。（an image of）
那幅画面成了小镇对自己的形象。（image of itself）
档案馆的形象原本指望有点值得庆祝的东西。（image）
answers: For eleven weeks the local paper printed one image a week.
Nobody could image what the box was doing there.
There was no image of a clock in any of them to fix the date.
That image became the town's image of itself.
A photograph is an image and not an argument.
The image of the archive had been hoping for something celebratory.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 image 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: For eleven weeks the local paper printed one image a week, and nobody could image why the box was there.
There was no image of a clock in any of the plates, so the dates had to be worked outwards from a shop sign.
The image people remembered was not a street but a girl on a bicycle who never looks at the camera.
In about a month she became the town's image of itself: cheerful, unhurried, slightly out of focus.
A photograph is an image and not an argument; it proves that a thing was somewhere, never that it was fine.
An image, I have concluded, is not the past but what the past left on glass when nobody was watching.
